name: incumbent framing + stay-invested + hold_redeploy (stranded-cash fix)
description: Identical to fresh_news_hold_incumbent_invested.json except rebalance_mode=hold_redeploy. A one-variable test of whether fixing stranded exit proceeds rescues the incumbent framing.
notes: WHY THIS EXISTS: the incumbent framing produced the BEST selection skill of any
arm and still lost, because it hoarded cash. Two rounds of diagnosis:
ROUND 1 - blamed the prompt. The reset wording said leftover weight held as
cash is 'perfectly acceptable', and the incumbent task block never said to stay
invested. Fixed both -> hold_incumbent_invested. Cash moved 7.06% -> 6.51%,
p=0.48. NOT SIGNIFICANT. The fix did essentially nothing.
ROUND 2 - it was never the prompt. execute_hold_mode sells dropped names into
cash and then only ever spends that cash on names NOT already held. A decision
that drops a name without adding one strands the proceeds permanently. There is
no code path for 'put it into what I already own', so no prompt wording could
have reached it.
decisions that dropped >0 and added 0, and the cash they left:
hold_winners              25 / 540  (5%)    15.4%? no - 6.61% vs 0.01% elsewhere
hold_incumbent           199 / 540 (37%)    15.36% vs 2.05% elsewhere
hold_incumbent_invested  196 / 540 (36%)    15.50% vs 2.91% elsewhere
The incumbent framing made the model reluctant to ADD (adds 2.04 -> 0.48 per
decision), so it hit the stranding path 7x more often than the reset framing.
That is the whole cash story.
WHAT hold_redeploy CHANGES: after the normal exits and entries, leftover cash
tops up KEPT positions that sit BELOW their target weight, pro-rata to shortfall.
It never trims, so a position that compounded past its target is left alone and
the let-winners-run property hold mode exists for is preserved. Cash the model
deliberately asked for (weights summing under 1) still survives, because a book
already at target has no shortfall. Unit-tested on all four cases.
ONE VARIABLE: everything here matches fresh_news_hold_incumbent_invested.json
except rebalance_mode and results_subdir. If cash falls toward hold_winners'
1.52% and vs-INIT improves, the incumbent framing was right all along and the
engine was the problem. If cash falls but returns do NOT improve, the framing is
genuinely worse and the cash was a red herring.
WORTH RUNNING NEXT EITHER WAY: reset framing + hold_redeploy. hold_winners is the
best arm and still strands proceeds on 5% of its decisions, so the fix should help
it too - independently of anything to do with the incumbent framing.
threads=8: the limiter (_OAI_MIN_GAP_S=1.0, ~60 RPM global) binds at ~10.2
threads and 4 threads measured 3.99x parallelism at 23.5 RPM. The earlier stall
at threads=10 was the account running OUT OF CREDITS, not concurrency - confirmed
by a direct API probe. 8 leaves margin without giving up much speed.
dry_run is FALSE: this preset SPENDS BUDGET the moment it is started.
